title: NSN cycling team withdraws from Volta a Portugal following Finlay Tarling's death
dek: NSN's development squad withdrew from the Volta a Portugal on Saturday, one day after 19-year-old Welsh time-trial specialist Finlay Tarling died in a Friday incident involving a car that entered the race course.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Finlay Tarling, 19, from Wales, died Friday when local media reports indicated a car struck him after entering the road going opposite the race direction.
bottom_line: Watch for statements from race organizers on safety procedures and whether any changes will be implemented for remaining stages of the Volta a Portugal or future events. Any findings from authorities investigating the incident would also clarify the sequence of events that led to the fatality.
body: NSN withdrew its development squad from the Volta a Portugal on Saturday, one day after the death of 19-year-old rider Finlay Tarling in an incident that occurred during Friday's stage.

Tarling, a Welsh cyclist and time-trial specialist, died in what race organizers described as a serious incident. According to local media reports cited by ESPN, a car entered the race road going in the opposite direction and struck Tarling. The driver reportedly missed the warning signs from race stewards positioned to manage traffic around the course.

In a statement reported by ESPN, NSN said the withdrawal occurred "with the full support of Fin's parents." The team also announced it would continue competing at the Czech Tour and the Arctic Race of Norway.

The fatal accident raises questions about the safety infrastructure at major European cycling events, including course marshaling, driver screening and communication, and emergency response protocols. The precise circumstances of how the vehicle breached the secured race perimeter and whether any investigation is underway have not been confirmed in the available materials.
